text.S1: There once was a married man and woman who wished for a child. At length the woman hoped God was about to grant her desire. These people had a little window at the back of their house from which a splendid garden could be seen, which was full of the most beautiful flowers and herbs. It was surrounded by a high wall, which no one dared to pass, because it belonged to an evil enchantress who had great power and was dreaded by all the world.
text.T1: Panali banja lina limene limafuna kukhala ndi mwana. Kwa nthawi yaitali mzimayi ameneyo amaganizira kuti Mulungu anali pafupi kuwapatsa cofunacawo. Anthu awa anali ndi kadzenera kumbuyo kwa nyumba yawo kumene dimba lokongola limawonekera, limene linali ndi maluwa okongola ndi zitsamba.Dimba limeneli linali lozungulidwa ndi cipupa cacitali,ndipo aliyense samayesa kudzerapo, cifukwa malo amenewo anali malo yamfiti yoyipa imene inali ndi mphamvu zoipa ndipo dziko lonse limacita nayo mantha mfitiyo.
text.T2: Panali banja lina limene limafuna kukhala ndi mwana. Kwa nthawi yaitali mzimayi ameneyo amaganizira kuti Mulungu anali pafupi kuwapatsa cofunacawo. Anthu awa anali ndi kazenera kumbuyo kwa nyumba yawo kumene dimba lokongola limawonekera, limene linali ndi maluwa okongola ndi zitsamba.Dimba limeneli linali lozungulidwa ndi cipupa cacitali,ndipo aliyense samayesa kudzerapo, cifukwa malo amenewo anali malo yamfiti yoyipa imene inali ndi mphamvu zoipa kwambiri ndipo dziko lonse limacita nayo mantha mfitiyo.

text.S1: One day the woman, who was standing by the window and looking down into the garden, which was planted with the most beautiful flower, named rapunzel. It looked so fresh and so green she wanted it and had the greatest desire to eat it. This desire increased everyday, and as she knew that she could not have any, she quietly languished, and looked pale and tired.
text.S2: One day when the woman was standing by the window, she was looking at the garden, which had the most beautiful flower, named rapunzel. The flower looked so fresh and green that she greatly desired to eat it. This desire increased every day, and as she knew that she could not have any, she quietly languished, and looked pale and tired.
text.T1: Tsiku lina pamene mzimayiyu ali ciyimire pambali padzenera, anali kupenya kudimba, lomwe munali duwa lokongola, lochedwa rapunzel. Duwa limenelo limawoneka latsopano ndi lamsipu ndipo amafunitsitsa kuti alidye. Cilakolako cake cimakula tsiku lililonse, ndipo anadziwa kuti sangakwanitse, ndipo anavutika mwakacetecete, ndipo amawoneka wofoka ndi wotopa.
text.T2: Tsiku lina pamene mzimayiyu ali ciyimire pambali pazenera, anali kupenya kudimba, lomwe munali duwa lokongola, lochedwa rapunzel. Duwa limenelo limawoneka latsopano ndi lamsipu ndipo amafunitsitsa kuti alidye. Cilakolako cake cimakula tsiku lililonse, ndipo anadziwa kuti sangakwanitse kukhala nalo, ndipo anavutika mwakacetecete, ndipo amawoneka wofoka ndi wotopa.

text.S1: She told the man: "If I can't get some of the rapunzel flower behind our house to eat, I shall die." And the man thought, “I will bring my wife some of the flower, let it cost what it will”. In the twilight of the evening, he clambered down over the wall into the garden of the evil enchantress, hastily grabbed a handful of rapunzels, and took them back to his wife. The woman made herself a salad of it, and ate it with joy.
text.S2: The woman told the man that: "If I can't get the rapunzel flower behind our house to eat, I shall die." The man thought, “At any cost, I will bring my wife some of the flower”. In the twilight of the evening, he climbed over the wall into the evil witch’s garden, hastily plucked some of the rapunzel flower, and took them back to his wife. The woman made herself a sumptuous meal, and ate it with joy.
text.T1: Mzimayi uja anauza mzibambo kuti: “Ngati sindingapeze maluwa a rapunzel kumbuyo kwanyumba yathu kuti ndidye, ndidzafa.’’ Mwamuna uja anaganiza, “Ndidzamubweretsera maluwa mkazi wanga, pa mtengo uliwonse, ndidzakwanitsa.’’ M’nthawi yacisisira, m’madzulo, mwamunayo anakwera cipupa ndi kulowa m’dimba momwe mumakhala mfiti yowopsa, ndipo mofulumira anathyola maluwa a rapunzel, ndi kum’perekera mkazi wake. Mkazi anapanga zakudya zotsekemera, ndipo anazidya ndi cimwemwe.
text.T2: Mzimayi uja anauza mzibambo kuti: “Ngati sindingapeze maluwa a rapunzel kumbuyo kwanyumba yathu kuti ndidye, ndidzafa.’’ Mwamuna uja anaganiza, “Ndidzamubweretsera maluwa mkazi wanga, pa mtengo wina uliwonse.’’ M’nthawi yacisisira, m’madzulo, mwamunayo anakwera cipupa ndi kulowa m’dimba momwe mumakhala mfiti yowopsa, ndipo mofulumira anathyola maluwa a rapunzel, ndi kum’perekera mkazi wake. Mkazi anapanga zakudya zotsekemera, ndipo anazidya ndi cimwemwe.

text.S1: She, however, liked it so much—so very much, that the next day she longed for it three times as much as before. Her husband must once more descend into the garden. In the gloom of evening, therefore, he let himself down again; but when he had clambered down the wall he was terribly afraid, for he saw the enchantress standing before him.
text.S2: She liked it so much that the next day she longed for it three times as much as the day before. Her husband must once more descend the wall into the garden. In the gloom of evening, therefore, he went into the garden again; but when he had clambered down the wall he was terribly afraid, because he saw the enchantress standing before him.
text.T1: Iye anakonda kudya maluwa a rapunzel kwambiri – kotero kuti, tsiku lotsatira amafuna maluwa oculuka katatu kuposa omwe anadya tsiku lapitalo. Mwamuna wake anatsikanso cipupa, kulowa m’dimba. Kuli mdima bii m’madzulo, cotero, iye anapitanso m’dimba; koma pamene anakwera cipupa cija movutikira anacita mantha kwambiri, cifukwa anawona mkazi wamatsenga ali cilili pafupinaye.
text.T2: Iye anakonda kudya maluwa a rapunzel kwambiri – kotero kuti, tsiku lotsatira amafuna maluwa oculuka katatu kuposa omwe anadya tsiku lapitalo. Mwamuna wake amafunikanso kutsika cipupa, kulowa m’dimba. Kuli mdima bii m’madzulo, cotero, iye anapitanso m’dimba; koma pamene anatsika cipupa cija movutikira anacita mantha kwambiri, cifukwa anawona mkazi wamatsenga ali cilili patsogolo pake.

text.S1: "How dare you," said the enchantress with a very angry look, "you descended into my garden and stole my rapunzels like a thief? You will suffer for it!" "Ah," answered the man. "Let mercy take the place of justice, I only made up my mind to do it out of necessity. My wife saw your flowers from the window, and felt such a longing for it she would have died if she had not had some."
text.S2: "How dare you," said the enchantress with a very angry look, "you entered into my garden and stole my rapunzels like a thief? You will suffer for it!" "Ah," answered the man. "Let mercy take the place of justice, I only made up my mind to do it out of necessity. My wife saw your flowers from the window, and felt such a longing for it she would have died if she had not had some."
text.T1: “Ukulimba mtima bwanji,’’ anatero mkazi wamatsenga uja, akupenyetsetsa momvetsa mantha kwambiri, “walowa m’dimba langa ndipo ndi kuba maluwa anga a rapunzel ngati munthu wakuba? Udzavutikirapo pa zimenezi!’’ “Haa,”anayankha mwamuna uja. “Ndicitireni cifundo m’malo mwacilungamo,ine ndinacita izi cifukwa cosowa cocita.Mkazi wanga anawona maluwa kupyolera padzenera, ndipo tinaganiza kuti cifukwa cofunitsitsa maluwa amenewo, mkazi wanga akanafa ngati sitinapeze aliwonse kuti adye.’’
text.T2: “Ukulimba mtima bwanji,’’ anatero mkazi wamatsenga uja, akupenyetsetsa momvetsa mantha kwambiri, “walowa m’dimba langa ndipo ndi kuba maluwa anga a rapunzel ngati mbala? Udzavutikirapo pa zimenezi!’’ “Haa,”anayankha mwamuna uja. “Ndicitireni cifundo m’malo mwacilungamo,ine ndinacita izi cifukwa cosowa cocita. Mkazi wanga anawona maluwa kupyolera pazenera, ndipo amafunitsitsa maluwa amenewo, mkazi wanga akanafa ngati sanapeze aliwonse kuti adye.’’

text.S1: Then the enchantress allowed her anger to be softened, and said to him, "If the case be as you say, I will allow you to take away with you as much rapunzel as you want, only I make a condition, you must give me the child which your wife will bring into the world. It will be well treated, and I will care for it like a mother." The man, in his terror, consented to everything, and when the woman was brought to bed, the enchantress appeared at once, named the child Rapunzel, and took her away.
text.S2: After that, the enchantress allowed her anger to be softened, and said to him, "If that is as you say it is, I will allow you to take away with you as much rapunzel as you want, only I make a condition, you must give me the child which your wife will give birth to. The child will be well treated, and I will care for it like a mother." The man, filled with terror, consented to everything the enchantress said, and when the woman had child, the enchantress appeared at once, named the child Rapunzel, and took her away that very moment.
text.T1: Pambuyo pake, mkazi wamatsenga uja analola kufewetsa mkwiyo wake pansi, ndipo anati kwa mwamunayo, “Ngati mlanduwu ungakhale monga mmene wanenera, ndidzakulola kutenga maluwa a rapunzel oculuka monga momwe ungakwanitsire, koma kokha ndipanga cotsatira, uyenera kundipatsa mwana amene mkazi adzabereke. Mwanayo adzasungidwa bwino, ndipo ndidzamusamalira ngati amayi ake.” Mwamuna uja, ali wodzadzidwa ndi mantha, analoleza kuzinthu zonse zomwe mkazi wamatsenga ananena. Pamene mkazi anakhala ndi mwana, mkazi wamatsenga anabwera nthawi yomweyo, ndikucha mwanayo dzina lakuti Rapunzel, ndipo anamtenga nthawi imeneyo.
text.T2: Pambuyo pake, mkazi wamatsenga uja analola kufewetsa mkwiyo wake, ndipo anati kwa mwamunayo, “Ngati zili monga mmene wanenera, ndidzakulola kutenga maluwa a rapunzel oculuka monga momwe ungafunire, koma kokha ndipanga cotsatira, uyenera kundipatsa mwana amene mkazi adzabereke. Mwanayo adzasungidwa bwino, ndipo ndidzamusamalira ngati amayi ake.” Mwamuna uja, ali wodzadzidwa ndi mantha, analoleza kuzinthu zonse zomwe mkazi wamatsenga ananena. Pamene mkazi anakhala ndi mwana, mkazi wamatsenga anabwera nthawi yomweyo, ndikucha mwanayo dzina lakuti Rapunzel, ndipo anamtenga nthawi imeneyo.

text.S1: Rapunzel grew into the most beautiful child beneath the sun. The enchantress raised her as her daughter but treated her very cruely. When she was twelve years old, the enchantress locked her in a tower in a forest, which had neither stairs nor doors. At the top was a little window. When the enchantress wanted to climb in, she placed herself under it and cried, "Rapunzel, Rapunzel, Let down your hair to me." Rapunzel had magnificent long hair, and when she heard the voice of the enchantress she let down her braids, winding them round one of the hooks of the window above, and the enchantress climbed up.
text.S2: Rapunzel grew into the most beautiful child in the whole world. The enchantress raised her as her daughter but treated her very cruely. When the child was twelve years old, the enchantress locked her in a tower in a forest, which had neither stairs nor doors. At the top of the tower was a little window. When the enchantress wanted to see inside, she went under it and cried, "Rapunzel, Rapunzel, Let down your hair to me." Rapunzel had magnificent long hair, and when she heard the voice of the enchantress she let down her braids, winding them round one of the hooks of the window above, and the enchantress used it to climb up.
text.T1: Rapunzel anakula ndi kukhala mwana wokongola kwambiri m’dziko lapansi. Mkazi wamatsenga uja anamulera ngati mwana wake wamkazi, koma amausunga mwankhanza kwambiri. Pamene mwana uja anakwanitsa zaka khumi ndi ziwiri, mkazi wamatsenga anamukhomera m’nyumba yansanja yaitali m’nkhalango, ndipo nyumbayo inalibe matanda kapena zitseko. Pamwamba pa nyumbayo panali dzenera laling’ono. Pamene mkazi wamatsenga amafuna kukwera kuti alowe m’kati, amapita munsi mwa nyumba ndi kuitana kuti, “Rapunzel, Rapunzel, lola kuti tsitsi lako litsikire pansi kwaine.”Rapunzel anali ndi tsitsi lalitali lodabwitsa, ndipo pamene anamva liwu la mkazi wamatsenga, amatsitsira pansi tsitsi lake lolukalo, lokhotakhota ngati mbedza kumbali imodzi pamwamba padzenera, ndipo mkazi wamatsengayo amagwiritsa nchito pokwera kupita pamwambapo.
text.T2: Rapunzel anakula ndi kukhala mwana wokongola kwambiri m’dziko lapansi. Mkazi wamatsenga uja anamulera ngati mwana wake wamkazi, koma amamusunga mwankhanza kwambiri. Pamene mwana uja anakwanitsa zaka khumi ndi ziwiri, mkazi wamatsenga anamukhomera m’nyumba yansanja yaitali m’nkhalango, imene inalibe matanda kapena zitseko. Pamwamba pa nyumbayo panali zenera laling’ono. Pamene mkazi wamatsenga amafuna kukwera kuti alowe m’kati, amapita munsi mwa nyumba ndi kuitana kuti, “Rapunzel, Rapunzel, tsitsa tsitsi lako pansi kwaine.”Rapunzel anali ndi tsitsi lalitali lodabwitsa, ndipo pamene anamva liwu la mkazi wamatsenga, amatsitsira pansi tsitsi lake lolukalo, nalipotozera pa cokola ca pamwamba pazenera, ndipo mkazi wamatsengayo amagwiritsa nchito pokwera kupita pamwambapo.

text.S1: After a few years locked in this tower, Rapunzel became miserable. She grew tired and bored of being locked away all these years. It came to pass that the King's son rode through the forest and saw the tower. He heard a song, which was so charming that he stood still and listened. This was Rapunzel, who in her solitude passed her time in letting her sweet voice resound. The King's son wanted to climb up to see her and looked for the door of the tower, but none was to be found. He rode home, but the singing had so deeply touched his heart that every day he went out into the forest alone and listened to it. Once when he was standing behind a tree, he saw the enchantress arrive and he heard how she cried, "Rapunzel, Rapunzel, Let down your hair."
text.S2: After a few years locked in this tower, Rapunzel became miserable. She grew tired and bored of being locked away all these years. It came to pass that the King's son rode through the forest and saw the tower. He heard a song, which was so captivating that the King’s son stood still and listened. The one singing was Rapunzel, who in her solitude passed her time in letting her sweet voice resound. The King's son wanted to climb up to see her and looked for the door, but never found it. He mounted his horse and went back home, but the singing had deeply touched his heart that every day he went out into the forest alone and listened to it. Once when he was standing behind a tree, he saw the enchantress coming and he heard how she cried, "Rapunzel, Rapunzel, Let down your hair."
text.T1: Pambuyo pazaka zowerengeka alicitsekere m’nsanja imeneyi, Rapunzel anadzakhala wovutika. Iye anatopa ndipo anagwa mphwayi pokhala wotsekeredwa zaka zonsezi.Ndiye zinacitika kuti pamene mwana wamfumu amapyola nkhalango atakwera pa hosi anawona nsanjayo. Iye anamvera nyimbo, imene inali yokoka mtima kwambiri kwa kuti mwana wa Mfumu ameneyo anaimirira kumvetsera. Munthu yemwe amaimba anali Rapunzel, pokhala yekha yekha amacotsa mphwayi poyimba ndi mawu onzuna omveka patali. Mwana wamfumu anafuna kukwera kuti amuwone ndipo anafuna citseko koma sanacipeze. Anakwera hosi lake kubwerera kunyumba, koma mayimbidwe aja anam’koka mtima kotero kuti tsiku lililonse amapita kunkhalango kukamvetsera. Tsiku lina pamene anali ciyimire kumbuyo kwamtengo, anawona mkazi wamatsenga akubwera ndipo anamvetsera mmene amakuwira, ‘’Rapunzel, Rapunzel, gwetsapansi tsitsi lako’’
text.T2: Pambuyo pazaka zowerengeka alicitsekere m’nsanja imeneyi, Rapunzel anadzakhala wovutika. Iye anatopa ndipo anagwa mphwayi pokhala wotsekeredwa zaka zonsezi. text.S1: Rapunzel let down the braids of her hair, and the enchantress climbed up to her. "I will do the same thing," he said, and the next day he went and cried, "Rapunzel, Rapunzel, Let down the hair." Immediately the hair fell down and the boy climbed up. At first Rapunzel was terribly frightened, by the man whose eyes she had never yet beheld. The King's son told her that in his heart he could have no rest, until he had saved her from the evil enchantress. Rapunzel lost her fear, and realized now she could escape the evil enchantress. And she said, "I will willingly go away with you, but I do not know how to get down. Bring with you a scarf of silk each time that you come here, and I will weave a ladder with it.”
text.S2: Rapunzel let down her braided hair, and the enchantress climbed up the tower. "I will do the same thing," he said, and the next day he went and cried, "Rapunzel, Rapunzel, Let down your hair." Immediately the hair fell down and the boy climbed up. At first Rapunzel was terribly frightened, by seeing eye to eye with a man whom she’s never seen. The King's son told her that in his heart he could have no rest, until he had saved her from the evil enchantress. Rapunzel immediately lost her fear by realising that she could escape the evil enchantress. And she said, "I will willingly go away with you, but I do not know how to get down. Bring with you a scarf of silk each time that you come here, and I will weave a ladder with it.”
text.T1: Rapunzel anagwetsa pansi tsitsi lake lolukidwa, ndipo mkazi wamatsenga uja anakwera kupita pamwamba pansanja ija. “Ndidzacita cimodzoimodzi nanenso,’’ anatero mwana waMfumu, ndipo tsikulotsatirapo anapita nid kukweza mawu, Rapunzel, Rapunzel, gwetsa pansi tsitsi lako’’ Nthawi yomweyo tsitsi linagwetsedwa pansi ndipo mnyamata anakwera. Poyamba Rapunzel anamva mantha kwambiri, kuwonana ndi maso ndi maso ndi munthu wamwamuna yemwe sanamuwonepo. Mwana wamfumu anamuuza kuti sanapeze mpumulo mu mtima mwake, mpaka atam’pulumutsa kucokera kwamkazi wamatsengayo. Pamenepo mantha a Rapunzel anatha, pozindikira kuti angakwanitse kumuthawa mkazi wamatsenga uja. Ndipo anati, “Mosakakamizidwa ndidzapitanawe, koma sindidziwa kuti ndingatsike bwanji. Udzibweretsa nsalu yasiluku nthawi iliyonse imene ubwera kuno, ndipo ine ndidzaluka matanda kucokera kunsaluyo.’’

text.S1: They agreed that he should come to her every evening, for the old woman came by day. The enchantress remarked nothing of this, until once Rapunzel said to her, "Tell me, mother, how it happens that you are so much heavier for me to draw up than the young King's son—he comes this evening." "Ah! you wicked brat," cried the enchantress "What do I hear you say! I thought I had separated you from all evil in the world, and now you have yet deceived me." In her anger she clutched Rapunzel's beautiful braids, wrapped them twice round her left hand, seized a pair of scissors with the right, and snip, snip, they were cut off, and the lovely braids lay on the ground. And she was so pitiless that she took poor Rapunzel into a desert where she had to live in great grief and misery.
text.S2: Rapunzel and the King’s son agreed that he should come to her every evening, for the old woman came by day. The enchantress knew nothing of this, until once Rapunzel said to her, "Tell me, mother, how it is that you are so much heavier on climbing than the young King's son—he will be coming this evening." "Ah! you wicked brat," cried the enchantress "What have you just said! I thought I had separated you from all evil in the world, and now you have deceived me." In her anger she clutched Rapunzel's beautiful braids, wrapped them twice round her left hand, seized a pair of scissors with the right, and snip, snip, they were cut off, and the lovely braids fell on the ground. And she was so pitiless that she took Rapunzel into a desert where she had to live in great grief and misery.
text.T1: Rapunzel ndi mwana waMfumu anagwirizana kuti azibwera m’madzulo muli monse, cifukwa nkhalamba ija imabwera m’masana. Mkazi wamatsenga uja sanadziwepo kanthu kalikonse pazonsezi, mpaka Rapunzel atamuuza, “Ndiuzeni,mayi wanga, mmene zilili kuti inu ndinu wolemera pokwera kusiyana ndi mwana waMfumu –amene adzabwera madzulo ano’’ “Eee, mwana woyipa iwe,’’ anakalipa mkazi wamatsenga uja, “Ukuti ciyani zomwe wanenazi! Ndimaganizira kuti ndinakulekanitsa kuzoipa zonse padziko lapansi, tsopano wandinamiza bodza.’’ Ali ndi ukali tero,anakulunga kawiri kudzanja lake lamanzere tsitsi labwino lomangidwa la Rapunzel, anatenga sizele ndi dzanja lake lamanja, gelu, gelu, linadulidwa, ndipo tsitsi lake lamaonekedwe abwino linagwera pansi. Ndipo analibe cifundo kotero kuti anamutenga Rapunzel ndi kupita naye kucipululu kumene amakhala wozunzidwa komanso wovutika.
text.T2: Rapunzel ndi mwana waMfumu anagwirizana kuti azibwera m’madzulo muli monse, cifukwa nkhalamba ija imabwera m’masana. Mkazi wamatsenga uja sanadziwepo kanthu kalikonse pazonsezi, mpaka Rapunzel atamuuza, “Ndiuzeni,mayi wanga, mmene zilili kuti inu ndinu wolemera pokwera kusiyana ndi mwana waMfumu –amene adzabwera madzulo ano’’ “Eee, mwana wopusa iwe,’’ anakalipa mkazi wamatsenga uja, “Ukuti ciyani zomwe wanenazi! Ndimaganizira kuti ndinakulekanitsa kuzoipa zonse zadziko lapansi, tsopano wandinamiza bodza.’’ Ali ndi ukali tero,anagwira tsitsi labwino lomangidwa la Rapunzel nalikulunga kawiri kudzanja lake lamanzere, anatenga cometera ndi dzanja lake lamanja, gelu, gelu, linadulidwa, ndipo tsitsi lake lamaonekedwe abwino linagwera pansi. Ndipo analibe cifundo kotero kuti anamutenga Rapunzel ndi kupita naye kucipululu kumene amakhala wozunzidwa komanso wovutika.

text.S1: On the same day, however, that she cast out Rapunzel, the enchantress fastened the braids of hair which she had cut off to the hook of the window, and when the King's son came and cried, "Rapunzel, Rapunzel, Let down your hair," she let Rapunzel’s hair down. The King's son ascended, but he did not find the dearest Rapunzel above, but the evil enchantress, who gazed at him with wicked and venomous looks. "Aha!" she cried mockingly, "You would find my dearest, but the beautiful bird sits no longer singing in the nest; the cat has got it, and will poke out your eyes as well. Rapunzel is gone; you will never see her again."

text.T1: Patsiku limodzimodzi limene anacotsera tsitsi lolukala Rapunzel, mkazi wamatsenga anamangirira zikondo zomwe anadula pazenera, ndipo pomwe mwana waMfumu anabwera anakweza mawu kuitana, “Rapunzel, Rapunzel, tsitsa tsitsi lako,” mkazi wamatsenga anatsitsadi tsitsi la Rapunzel. Mwana waMfumu anakwera pamwamba, koma sanapeze wokondedwa Rapunzel pamwambapo, koma anapeza mkazi wamatsenga woipa uja, yemwe anam’penyetsetsa ndimaso aululu, “Eya!” anatero monyoza. “Umabwera ndi kupeza wokondedwa wanga, koma mbalame yokongola ija siikhalanso pano ndi kumaimba m’cisa; mphaka anayitenga, ndipo mphakayo adzawononga maso ako nawenso.Rapunzel anapita; ndipo sudzamuwonanso."

text.S1: The King's son was beside himself with pain, and in his despair he leapt down from the tower. He escaped with his life, but the thorns into which he fell, pierced out his eyes. He wandered quite blind about in the forest, ate nothing, but roots and berries, and did nothing but lament and weep over the loss of his dearest love. Thus he roamed about in misery for some years, and at length came to the desert where Rapunzel lived in wretchedness. He heard a voice, and it seemed so familiar that he wept going towards it, and when he approached, Rapunzel knew him and fell to her knees and wept. Two tears wetted the prince’s eyes and they grew clear again, and he could see with them as before. He led her to his kingdom where he was joyfully received, and they lived for a long time afterwards, happy and content.
text.S2: The King's son was lonely filled with pain, and in his despair he leapt down from the tower. He escaped with his life, but the thorns where he fell, pierced out his eyes. He wandered whilst blind about in the forest, ate nothing, but roots and berries, and did nothing but lament and weep over the loss of his loved one. Thus he roamed about in misery for some years, and at length came to the desert where Rapunzel lived in wretchedness. He heard a voice, and it sounded familiar that he wept going towards it, and when he approached, Rapunzel knew him and fell to her knees and wept. Two tears fell on the prince’s eyes so much so that they grew clear again, and he could see with them as before. He led her to his kingdom where he was joyfully received, and they lived for a long time afterwards, happy and content.
text.T1: Mwanawa Mfumu anali pomwepo wodzadzidwa ndikupweteka, ndi wotayika mtima, analumphira pansi kucokera pansanja paja. Iye anathawa ndi moyo wake, minga pansi pomwe anagwera, inamutudzula maso ake. Iye anayendayenda ali ndi maso a khungu m’nkhalango muja, sanadye ciliconse koma amadya cabe mizu ndi zipatso, ndipo sanacite cina ciliconse kuposa kudandaula ndi kulira pakusoweka kwa pakusoweka kwa wokondedwa wake. Cotero, iye anazungulira movutika kwa zaka zingapo, ndipo pamtunda wautali, anafika kucipululu komwe Rapunzel amakhala mozunzika. Iye anamva liwu la, ndipo liwulo linamveka ngati ndi lodziwika kotero kuti analira potsendera pafupi, ndipo pomwe anali pafupi, Rapunzel anamudziwa ndipo anagwera pamawondo ake ndi kulira. Misozi iwiri inagwera pamaso a mwana waMfumu, kotero kuti maso ake anayeranso, ndipo anayambanso kupenya bwino ngati poyamba paja. Iye anamutsogolera ku ufumu wake, komwe anamulandira mwacisangalalo, ndipo anakhala moyo wautali pambuyo pake, okondwera ndi okhutira.
